title: Karnıyarık
subtitle: Turkish aubergines stuffed with spiced lamb mince
excerpt: Karniyarik means split belly in Turkish, and the dish earns the name: aubergines are fried until golden, split open, and filled with a rich, spiced lamb mince before being baked until everything melts together. It is a Turkish home-cooking classic and far more satisfying than it sounds on paper.
sourceNotes: A well-loved Turkish stuffed aubergine dish that appears regularly in home kitchens and lokanta restaurants. The name translates literally as split belly.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after baking. Reheat from frozen covered in a 160 C oven for 25 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The whole dish can be made a day ahead and reheated. Keeps well in the fridge for 2 days.

content.text: Karniyarik is the meatier sibling of imam bayildi. Where imam bayildi is vegan and delicate, karniyarik is robust and filling: fried aubergines piled with spiced lamb and baked until the whole thing is saucy and slightly charred at the edges.

The frying step is not optional. Pan-frying the aubergines before stuffing them gives the dish its characteristic colour and adds a depth of flavour that oven-roasting does not replicate. Use enough oil; an aubergine that has not absorbed enough fat will be dry and bland.
A slice of fresh tomato and a strip of green pepper laid over the top before baking is the traditional garnish. They soften and slightly char during baking and add freshness to the finished dish.

items.prepNote: one chopped for filling, one sliced for garnish

content.text: Peel the aubergines in alternating strips. Score deeply down the middle lengthways and salt the cut sides. Leave for 15 minutes, then pat dry. Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the aubergines for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and softened. Transfer to the baking tin. Press the slit open to create a cavity for the filling.

Preheat the oven to 190 C. In the same pan over medium heat, add 2 tbsp olive oil. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and green pepper and cook for 3 minutes. Add the lamb mince and break it up. Cook for 5 minutes until browned. Stir in the chopped tomato, tomato puree, paprika, allspice, parsley, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes until the mixture is fragrant and reduced.

Spoon the lamb filling generously into each aubergine cavity; it should overflow slightly. Top each with a slice of fresh tomato. Pour the stock around the aubergines. Cover the tin with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes until the tops are lightly browned. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

rows.cause: Not enough oil when frying or stock evaporated
rows.fix: Fry generously and add more stock during baking if the tin looks dry.

rows.cause: Lamb overcooked before baking or too lean
rows.fix: Stop cooking the filling when it is just cooked; it continues to cook in the oven. Use lamb with some fat content.
Fry until clearly golden and yielding; the skin needs to soften in the oil before baking.

content.text: Replace the lamb with beef mince for a different but equally good result. Add a pinch of dried chilli to the filling if you prefer more heat. Some versions include pine nuts stirred into the lamb for extra texture.
Karniyarik reheats well. Make the whole dish up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Cover with foil and reheat at 160 C for 20 minutes until piping hot.

Karniyarik is a Turkish household dish found in lokanta restaurants and home kitchens alike. It is served with rice or bread and yoghurt on the side. The dish has its roots in Ottoman palace cooking and has remained unchanged in Turkish domestic cooking for generations.
